ratings_why.fun: Clean curve: Duel bodies win early, Elder and Marshal grow the middle, and three Tier 6 payoffs all feed one Champion you get to watch get absurd.
ratings_why.distinct: Leaving gaps on purpose (Proud, empty-slot pay) and a pre-fight Duel rite play unlike any of today's tribes, though 'grow your biggest' and Start of Combat pings are familiar.

verdict_why: The shape is good, but a few rules don't read (Cork-Pop against 'Twice a fight', Duels into an empty front row) and Refectory Prior is a free pick early.

points.text: Master of the Cork-Pop doubles Sir Hartmut's re-Duel, but Hartmut is capped 'Twice a fight'. Say whether the extra trigger counts against the cap.
Herald of the Last Dawn and Sir Hartmut Duel 'a random front-row enemy'. Say what happens once the front row is dead: fall to the back row, or stop.
Refectory Prior pays every board on turns 2 to 4, so it's always the right buy early. Tie it to the tribe's shape, such as 'if you have 2 or more empty slots after Tier 3' or per Proud unit.
A two-unit board wins fights but deals almost no hero damage. A small hook, such as the Champion counting as 3 survivors, would make the Last Knight pay off in Health as well as fights.
The Chronicler needing 4 units while Elder wants few is a good puzzle. A 'you may' version keeps it and avoids the feel-bad turn.

standouts.why: Sir Gottfried is a real capstone: the whole Last Knight build points at him, and an empty board turning into a giant is the fantasy in one card.
Elder of the Centre makes empty slots pay every turn, so shrinking becomes the engine from Tier 3.
Sir Altmark grows off the enemy's size, so the Champion keeps pace with the lobby instead of with your own board.

weakest.why: Sprucehold Envoy is a generic Discover with a light board-size nod.
Pennon-Squire's +1/+1 and Duel is thin for Tier 2; it's mostly a splash tool.
Fantail Warden gives one Shield and has to stand alone to do it, so it costs a whole Proud slot.

flags.note: Alone he fights at x4 (x7 golden) on an already-fed Champion; the designer's 'beyond the second slot' fallback is ready if it runs away.
With Cork-Pop and Herald's three Duels, the Champion banks up to half of several enemies each fight, and the bigger Champion wins more Duels next fight.
Herald plus Hartmut, Brennbart and Ottokar's free first Duels could clear a front row before the first attack.
Golden Chronicler gives four times a grown Konrad each turn; bounded by what you feed it, but steep.
Doubling a trigger whose card says 'Twice a fight': does each doubled trigger use up the cap?
'A quarter of the loser's stats': its stats when it died, or before the Duel's damage?
Free gold for every board early; the designer flags it too.
